question: Does gate Option A (FLOW census measured at fixed pct=100, single pin 3593/a19f95a8) hold on the full guest-browser profile, and does the new #108 process-phase instrumentation fire correctly?

implementation.commit: b78b33a kernel: pin the FLOW census at pct=100 and name the #108 wait-loop silence point

files.os/aiueos/scripts/smoke-qemu-uefi.sh: treats the PROCESS_PHASE prefix as the #108 signature

run2-full-profile-probe-off.head: b78b33a
run2-full-profile-probe-off.profile: guest-browser full (AIUEOS_GUEST_BROWSER=1, synthetic=0), real virtio-keyboard + virtio-tablet via QMP
run2-full-profile-probe-off.scale: user scale ends pct=125 (SETTINGS persists); FLOW pins first: AIUEOS_GUEST_BROWSER_FLOW_SCALE pinned=100 prev=125

op-stream.re-measured-this-tick: sha1 of the words hex string recomputed from option-a-run2-flow-process-phase.log

process-phase-instrumentation.WAIT: wakes=1 timer=13 flush=2 result=1 sched=0 kotoba=42 worker=42 ipc=0 objwrite=1 (all exit predicates resolve on one wake)
process-phase-instrumentation.verified: instrumentation live; #108 stall NOT reproduced (see boundary)

run2-full-profile-probe-off.termination: GUEST-NO-EXIT after 505s: quiescence watchdog after 154s with no byte on either transport (limit 150s, last byte T+351s) = persistent loop normal terminal; last marker AIUEOS_DESKTOP_LOOP_OK persistent input service; harness marks NOT kotoba-lang/aiueos#108 (that hang stops at AIUEOS_KOTOBA_ELF_PROCESS_OK). SMOKE-EXIT=1 is the watchdog timeout, not a gate failure.

run1-not-evidence.head: c29f42e (pre-fix)
run1-not-evidence.result: harness wall budget 420s cut the run at the EDIT stage (EDIT n=48); partial logs kept in build/option-a-run1*.log

verdict: Option A green on the full profile: one canonical pin 3593/a19f95a8 is held by the pinned-pct measurement across runs whose user scale ends at pct=125; the op stream is byte-identical to every prior cell; the #108 phase instrumentation is live (all predicates observed, immediate reap).
boundary: kernel/*.c is still compiled by zig cc; the C-free claim covers the compiler lineage and the kotoba object route only. The #108 process-phase stall is not reproduced here - what is verified is the instrumentation and the named silence point, not a fix for #108. run2's SMOKE-EXIT=1 is the quiescence watchdog ending a persistent-loop run after 505s; the guest completed the whole suite.
